newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: INSTANT VIEW -Easing door ajar after NZ jobs data.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW -Easing door ajar after NZ jobs data.

text.p: Surprisingly low New Zealand employment growth at negative 0.5 percent in the December quarter was consistent with the economy slowing, leaving the door ajar for a further easing in monetary policy, economists said on Tuesday.
The unemployment rate dropped to 5.9 percent from 6.3 percent, and employment growth in the year fell to 2.1 percent from 3.7 percent at September 30.
Economists polled by Reuters on average expected seasonally adjusted quarterly employment growth of 0.325 percent, with forecasts ranging from zero to 0.6 percent.
DEUTSCHE MORGAN GRENFELL CHIEF ECONOMIST ULF SCHOEFISCH
"It was certainly a surprise. The market had expected between zero and 0.6 percent.

"It confirms that the economy was very weak towards the end of the last year. I would think the economy was a little weaker than also the Reserve Bank had expected and that is probably good news for the inflation prospects.
"If you work along the bank's two-to-one trade-off line, conditions have recently been tighter than that line suggested so I think short rates could rally a bit on this.
"Looking further ahead I think there is scope for some mild further easing by the bank.
The lower unemployment rate could be explained by the sharp fall in the participation rate to 65.5 percent from 66.4 percent.

He said he was sceptical of the participation rate numbers, with a sharp fall in part-time employment against a sharp rise in the September quarter. Part-time employment fell 5.0 percent in the quarter.
"One has to be a little suspicious of the precision of the measurement. I don't want to read to much into this."
